title: Meta and BlackRock Launch $14 Billion AI Data Center Venture in Texas
excerpt: The joint venture will build a one-gigawatt campus in El Paso, with BlackRock funds holding 80% ownership and $12.5 billion in debt financing backed by Meta's lease guarantees.
body:
• Meta and BlackRock announced a roughly $14 billion joint venture to build a one-gigawatt AI data center campus in El Paso, Texas, with BlackRock-managed funds holding 80% and Meta retaining 20%.
  • The financing includes $12.5 billion in debt arranged through a special vehicle called Sopaipilla Investor LLC, with the bonds receiving a preliminary A+ rating from S&P.
  • Meta will lease the entire facility while providing residual-value guarantees of about $13 billion, keeping substantial risk exposure despite offloading most ownership.
  • The deal follows Meta's $27 billion Hyperion campus venture with Blue Owl in Louisiana, establishing a repeatable model for financing AI infrastructure through managed funds and debt markets.

How the Deal Works

Meta will contribute land and construction already underway, valued at about $2.3 billion, while BlackRock-managed funds will put in approximately $4.9 billion in cash. Meta will also receive a $1 billion distribution to align the ownership split. The campus, designed for one gigawatt of compute capacity, is expected to begin coming online in 2028.

https://x.com/AlphaWireNewsAi/status/2089355691991716275

Rather than directly owning and financing the facility, Meta will lease the entire campus on a four-year initial term with four extension options stretching as long as 20 years. Meta will be the sole occupant and will provide construction, administrative, and property-management services.

"Building the infrastructure for superintelligence is key."

— Mark Zuckerberg, CEO, Meta Platforms

The debt component is being raised through Sopaipilla Investor LLC, a specialized holding vehicle. JPMorgan Chase and Morgan Stanley are arranging the bond sale, which received a preliminary A+ rating from S&P — a sign that traditional fixed-income investors are eager to fund AI infrastructure and unlocking a vast pool of sidelined capital, according to MarketBeat analysis.

Risk Stays Close to Meta

Despite offloading 80% of the property to managed funds, Meta retains significant financial exposure. The company is providing residual-value guarantees with an aggregate threshold of about $13 billion that decline over time. If the venture's assets fall short of fair value within 16 years, Meta would cover the gap.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=8XBauYUwHDo

"This is not a clean transfer of risk from Meta to BlackRock," noted an analysis from Immortal AI. "Meta remains the tenant, the operating brain of the project and a major source of credit support. The structure reduces the amount of property Meta must own and fund directly, but it works because lenders and investors believe Meta will keep paying."

Lenders and investors are essentially betting on Meta's long-term financial strength and continued demand for AI computing. The 80% ownership by BlackRock funds is held through its Global Infrastructure Partners and HPS Investment Partners divisions, with the ultimate economic risk sitting primarily with the underlying fund investors rather than BlackRock's own balance sheet.

A Wider Financing Trend

The El Paso campus is not Meta's first transaction of this kind. In October 2025, the company announced a similar venture for its Hyperion campus in Louisiana, where Blue Owl-managed funds took 80% and Meta kept 20%, funding approximately $27 billion in development costs. Together, the two deals establish a repeatable financing model for AI infrastructure — the tech company supplies demand and credit support while managed funds and debt markets supply most of the property capital.

AI-related bond issuance reached $270 billion by early July 2026, nearly twice the total raised in all of 2025, according to Bank of America data cited by Reuters. The figures underscore how technology companies are increasingly combining corporate spending with external financing to fund what Meta CEO Mark Zuckerberg has described as the infrastructure needed for "superintelligence."

Questions About the Public Bill

The financing story extends beyond private capital. El Paso has granted the project an 80% abatement of certain city property taxes for ten years, along with grants equal to 80% of applicable city property-tax revenue for 15 years. The city also waived multiple development and permit fees and allowed up to $7.5 million in road reimbursement.

Meta projects more than 4,000 construction jobs and 300 permanent operating jobs. However, the existing local incentive agreements require just 50 full-time jobs across all phases combined — a gap between promotional claims and contractual commitments that community advocates say deserves scrutiny.

"The scale of spending still raises valid questions about cash flow, future operating costs, and investment returns, particularly as Meta doesn't have a large cloud business selling spare capacity to external customers," said Matt Britzman, senior equity analyst at Hargreaves Lansdown.

Meta shares have fallen about 10% this year as investors scrutinize the costs of AI expansion. The company was scheduled to report second-quarter results on July 29.
nri_angle: Meta's massive AI infrastructure bet could reshape the tech employment landscape in Texas, a growing hub for Indian-American tech workers drawn by lower costs and booming data center construction.
author: Diaspora Desk
